new_statements.translation: Besides its six citation tones, Shaowu also has a neutral (light) tone. The pitch of the neutral tone is a mid short 13 after yangqu (35) and a low, short 11 elsewhere. Neutral-tone syllables are quite widespread, which is rare among Fujian dialects. Neutral tone is read mainly in the following contexts (neutral-tone syllables are left unmarked for tone in the transcriptions below): 1. the noun suffixes zi, er, tou, lao …; 2. the particles ge and de …; 3. the localizers di, shang, xia, tou …; 4. the pronominal suffixes duo, er, kuai …; 5. the directional verbs lai, qu etc. …; 6. the sentence-final particles ne, ma, le etc. …; 7. the second syllable of a considerable proportion of disyllabic words is read in the neutral tone, e.g. 'tail' mei⁵ pa, 'ability' pən⁵ sə, 'doctor' i¹ sen, 'bucket' suei³ t'oŋ …

new_statements.rule_in_words: Shaowu is a six-tone language (阴平21 阳平33 上声55 阴去213 阳去35 入声53). The only stress-related statement is about the neutral/light tone (轻声), i.e. toneless, reduced syllables: grammatical morphemes (noun suffixes, particles 个/得, localizers, pronominal suffixes, directional 来/去, sentence-final particles) and the second syllable of many disyllabic lexical words are unstressed/toneless, their pitch being set by the preceding tone (13 after yangqu, 11 elsewhere in the 1998 provincial gazetteer; a three-way high/mid/low conditioning by the preceding tone in the 1993 city gazetteer). Which syllable is light is lexically/morphologically determined, not positional; neither source uses the term 重音 (stress) or says where prominence falls in words without a light syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: 邵武市志 notes the light syllable after 上声 is slightly higher than after 阳平 but is merged with it for transcription convenience; its rule text lists 阳平 twice (once as mid, once as low) where the examples show the low class is after 阴平 and 入声 — an evident typo. 方言志 adds that tone sandhi (连读变调) applies in fast speech but not when words are read in list/citation style, and applies to coordinate/modifier-head/verb-complement compounds, not to subject-predicate or verb-object phrases.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about 轻声 (neutral tone / light syllables), the Chinese-dialectological correlate of unstressed syllables, not about 重音 in so many words; domain is the phonological word/compound (disyllabic and trisyllabic words) plus enclitic particles at phrase level; citation forms carry one of six full tones. Reading 'tone language with a stress statement' should be understood as 'tonal, with a neutral-tone (unstressed-syllable) statement'; a reviewer may prefer 'tone language, no stress statement'.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Both quoted gazetteers describe the Shaowu city (城关) dialect 邵武话, the representative variety of Glottolog's shao1234 'Shaojiang Chinese' (ISO sjc), which also covers Guangze, Jiangle, Shunchang etc; the 方言志 chapter additionally compares 光泽/建宁/泰宁/将乐/明溪 (第三节). Ngai 2021 likewise describes Shaowu city. Note the two gazetteers differ on the neutral-tone pitch (1998: 13 after 阳去, else 11; 1993: three levels high/mid/low by preceding tone) and on 阳平 (33 vs 22).

tone_statements.citation: 陳忠敏 [Chen Zhongmin]. 1993. 邵武方言入聲化字的實質 [The real nature of the 'rushenghua' words (words shifted into the entering tone) in the Shaowu dialect]. 中央研究院歷史語言研究所集刊 (Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica) 63(4): 815-830.
tone_statements.quote: 福建邵武方言的單字調共有六類（陳章太 1984）：陰平 21、陽平 22、上聲 55、陰去 213、陽去 35、入聲 53。入聲沒有塞韻尾，但讀音比較短促，同舒聲有明顯的區別。… 古入聲清聲母字今讀入聲；古入聲次濁、全濁聲母字今一般讀陽去。這是一般規律。除此之外，有一特殊情況：古平聲清濁聲母字、古上聲清、次濁、全濁聲母字，古去聲清濁聲母字，古入聲濁聲母字都有一些字今邵武方言讀入聲，其中尤以古平聲濁聲母字、古入聲濁聲母字爲多。我們稱這部分字爲入聲化字，其他今讀入聲（即古入聲清聲母字）稱原入聲字。
tone_statements.translation: The citation tones of the Shaowu dialect of Fujian fall into six categories (Chen Zhangtai 1984): yinping 21, yangping 22, shangsheng 55, yinqu 213, yangqu 35, rusheng 53. The entering tone has no stop coda, but it is pronounced rather short and is clearly distinct from the non-entering tones. ... MC entering-tone words with voiceless initials are read in the entering tone today; MC entering-tone words with sonorant or voiced-obstruent initials are generally read yangqu. This is the general rule. Beyond it there is a special case: some words from MC ping (voiceless and voiced), shang (voiceless, sonorant, voiced), qu (voiceless and voiced) and voiced ru categories are read in the entering tone in Shaowu today, especially MC voiced-initial ping and voiced-initial ru words. We call these 'rushenghua' (entering-tone-ised) words; the other entering-tone words (MC voiceless-initial ru) we call original entering-tone words.

tone_statements.n_tones: 6 citation tones (21, 22, 55, 213, 35, 53); 入声 53 short, no stop coda

tone_statements.quote: The Shaowu dialect has six tones as shown below. Tones will be indicated with the diacritics given in the examples. 1. inpyng; very low, slightly falling, [21]: tièn 癲 'crazy' ... 2. yangpyng; low level, [22]: thōng 腸 'intestines' ... 3. shaangsheng; high level, [55]: siŏng 想 'thinks' ... 5. inchiuh; low rising, [213]: tšǎ 蔗 'sugarcane' ... 6. yangchiuh; high rising, [35]: ní 二 'two' ... 7. inruh; high falling, [52]: piê 八 'eight' ... Atonic or so-called neutral tone syllables are a prominent feature of Shaowu ... Shaowu possesses one case of tone sandhi.

tone_statements.summary: Six tones (2 level, 4 contour), numbered etymologically; neutral-tone syllables prominent; one sandhi: inshaang 55 turns falling before suffixes -ə/-tsə (older value, Walker 1878). Nothing on stress.

sources.note: zh: 「邵武話的輕聲的實際調值有高、中、低三種，由其前字決定。在陰去、陽去之後為高調，陽平、上聲之後為中調（其中上聲之後的略高些），陰平、入聲之後為低調。」 and 「邵武話也存在連讀變調和聲母類化的現象。」 — a paraphrase of 邵武市志, citing the fjsq.gov.cn pages that led to the primary texts above. en: tone table only, cites Ngai 2021; nothing on stress.

sources.note: 第一节 轻声 (index1661): 「邵武话的轻声变化是比较普遍的，并且有一定的规律性，但它的词汇、语法意义却不十分重要。」 一、轻声调值 (img1168): 「邵武话轻声的调值大体可分为高、中、低三类。在阴去［④］、阳去［⑤］之后最高，用5来表示；在阳平［②］、上声［③］之后中高，用3来表示，上声之后的轻声调值比在阳平之后稍高，为了记音的方便而把它们归并在一类；在阳平［②］［sic — the example heading reads 阴平］、入声［⑥］之后最低，用1表示。」 followed by disyllabic examples and trisyllabic patterns (final syllable light, medial syllable light, last two syllables light). Neutral-tone pitch is thus determined by the preceding tone; no 重音 statement.

sources.note: States the six citation tones of Shaowu (阴平 21, 阳平 22, 上声 55, 阴去 213, 阳去 35, 入声 53; the 入声 has no stop coda but is audibly short and distinct from the other tones), tabulates their Middle-Chinese correspondences (MC voiced 入 > 阳去 etc.), then analyses the '入声化' words - items from MC 平/上/去 and voiced 入 categories that are read in the 53 entering tone - arguing they are a fossilised glottal-stop diminutive (ʔ化小称) tone change rather than dialect mixture or an initial-conditioned split; compares Wu, Gan-Hakka, Yue and Min diminutive tone change.
